title: Introduce Fleet Headroom Controller and priority-based drain signal
author: Aisha Banerjee
description:
Motivation: We observed tail latency degradation and failed requests during short-lived traffic surges when capacity was consumed by a few busy tenants. Existing burst tokens and autoscaler rules react after utilization climbs, which can cause transient SLA misses. This PR introduces a proactive "Fleet Headroom Controller" that tracks per-fleet headroom budgets and issues a priority-based drain signal to the router and scheduler to enable graceful preemptive scaling and tenant draining when headroom drops below configured thresholds.

Summary of changes: Adds a controller component in the fleet manager that computes headroom forecasts, exposes new telemetry, and emits drain/hold signals scoped by priority tier. The controller integrates with the autoscaler to request tentative scale actions (scale-up hints) before hard saturation and with the scheduler to mark pods for low-impact draining. The router uses the drain signal to shift best-effort or low-priority traffic to fallback models or lower-cost capacity.

Design notes: The headroom controller maintains an exponentially-weighted moving average of active concurrency, queued request depth, and per-tenant token consumption. It computes a conservative headroom estimate (tokens available that won’t violate throughput SLAs) and evaluates three thresholds: warning, proactive, and critical. When proactive is hit, the controller: 1) submits a scale-hint with desired additional replicas in the Dedicated autoscaler API, and 2) emits a per-tenant drain_score signal (0..100) to the scheduler/router for low-cost eviction/drain ordering. The drain_score is weighted by tenant priority, recent error budget consumption, and model size.

Backward compatibility: Controller defaults are off and guarded by a feature flag (fleet.headroom.enabled=false). When enabled, behavior is opt-in per-fleet via the dedicated fleet CRD (fleet.spec.headroom: {enabled, target_slo_ms, proactive_threshold_pct}). Existing autoscaler and router behavior remains unchanged unless the drain signal is observed.

Telemetry and observability: New Prometheus metrics and traces included: redwood_fleet_headroom_available_tokens, redwood_fleet_headroom_forecast_seconds, redwood_headroom_scale_hints_total{reason}, redwood_headroom_drain_events_total{priority}, and per-tenant headroom_score gauge (labels: tenant_id, priority). Grafana dashboards updated with a "Headroom" panel and a heatmap for drain pressure across tenants. Alerting: alert rule headroom_critical_for_60s triggers P2 and suggests immediate scale-up or capacity reallocation.

Configuration example (fleet CRD snippet):

fleet.spec.headroom: |
  enabled: true
  target_slo_ms: 150
  proactive_threshold_pct: 70  # start hinting when 70% of conservative headroom used

Tests and validation: Unit tests for EWMA and threshold logic; e2e simulation harness in benchmark-lab/sim that replays tenant traffic spikes to validate: (1) scale-hint issued before saturation, (2) router respects drain_score for low-priority tenants, (3) no noisy scaling churn for stable traffic. Load test run against a 50-node Dedicated cluster: proactive mode reduced 95th percentile latency regressions by ~22% during short surges compared to baseline.

Changeset (high level): implement controller in fleet manager (go), autoscaler API extension for scale-hints (proto + server), router/drain signal plumbing, scheduler drain ordering, Prometheus metrics and Grafana dashboard updates, helm chart flags, unit/e2e tests, docs.

Rollout plan: feature-flag gated -> internal dogfood in staging -> enable for a small number of Dedicated customers with opt-in -> monitor headroom metrics and rollback if unexpected churn. Recommended rollout uses canary percentage on fleet CRD.

Security and cost: No new customer-facing credentials. Scale hints are advisory; autoscaler still makes final decisions, preventing malicious headroom requests. Cost impacts are configurable via proactive_threshold_pct and max_scale_hint_replicas.

Why this is different: Existing burst token and autoscaler work react after capacity pressure; headroom controller aims to make safe, conservative preemptive moves to avoid SLA violations while preserving cost controls.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for EWMA and scoring - [x] Integration tests for router/scheduler plumbing - [x] Prometheus metrics + dashboards - [x] Feature flag + helm chart values - [x] Docs update in redwood-docs/ops/fleet-headroom.md

Related: Linear ENG-4897, ENG-5063. Jira SUP-1812 (support case where tenant experienced repeated transient errors during surge).
